title: Evenness is yoga
hook: evenness of mind is called yoga (Bhagavad Gita 2.48)
tomorrow: how does someone steady in wisdom actually walk and talk?

segments.voice: Yesterday the Sermon on the Mount ended on the rock: hearing and doing. Today a new book opens, and a very different place: the edge of a battlefield.
screen: `ON THE ROCK.` → `A NEW BOOK: THE GITA.`

segments.voice: Refreshing the inbox after an interview. Watching the dots while someone types. The work is done, and the result isn't yours yet. That's yesterday's question, and the Bhagavad Gita opens in that exact seat. A blind king, far from the fighting, asks his advisor Sanjaya to tell him what's happening on the field of Kurukshetra: what are my sons and the sons of Pandu doing? He can't see it. He can't change it. He can only wait for the report.
screen: `REFRESHING THE INBOX.` → `A BLIND KING, WAITING.` → `WHAT ARE THEY DOING?`

segments.voice: The report Sanjaya gives is a conversation. On the field, the archer Arjuna loses heart before a war against his own family, and his charioteer Krishna, whom many Hindus revere as God, answers him. Krishna doesn't promise him a good result. He changes what Arjuna is holding on to. Here's the heart of the answer, in chapter two. Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Don't let the fruit be your motive, and don't cling to doing nothing either. Then: steady in yoga, do your work, letting go of attachment, the same in success and in failure. And the definition: evenness is called yoga. In Sanskrit, samatvam yoga uchyate. One to tell a friend: in this verse, yoga isn't a pose on a mat. It's a mind that stays level whichever way the result falls. That's the teaching Hindus call karma yoga, the yoga of action: do your duty fully, and let go of the fruit. It isn't the same as not caring. Arjuna still has to act; the Gita is plain that doing nothing is no way out. What changes is where he stands while the result is still out: not on the result, but on the work. The blind king waits for news. The one doing the work can be even.
screen: `ARJUNA LOSES HEART.` · `THE WORK IS YOURS, NOT THE FRUIT.` · `EVENNESS IS CALLED YOGA.` · `KARMA YOGA: ACT, LET GO.` · then, large: `EVENNESS.`

segments.voice: Name one result you're waiting on right now. Say to yourself, quietly, what your part is, the work, and what isn't, the outcome. Then breathe evenly, the same count in and out, and let both sit side by side.
Evenness is yoga: Krishna's definition in the Gita, a mind that stays level in success and in failure while the work goes on.
Keep this one: evenness, the work yours and the fruit not. The Gita is open now, and the king is still waiting.

howItsDone: Hindus read Bhagavad Gita 2.47–48 as the core of karma yoga, the yoga of action: doing one's duty fully without attachment to its results; the verses are recited and taught in homes, temples and Gita study groups.

fork.setup: your cousin trained for months for a marathon and woke up sick on race day. what does evenness say?
options: the training was her part and still counts; meet this result evenly, and keep going.
the months were wasted if she can't run; the result is all that matters.
she should stop setting goals, so nothing can ever upset her again.
fork.reveal: the work is yours, the fruit isn't. evenness isn't giving up; it's staying level and acting again.

what a scholar hears: Gita 2.47–48, the root of what Hindus call karma yoga, framed as Sanjaya's report to the blind king Dhritarashtra.
guess: a mind level in success and failure, called yoga in the Gita

chat.says: interview done. they said they'd call by friday. i've refreshed my email forty times
options: Your part was the interview, and it's done. The Gita says stay even either way, and keep going.
If they don't call, the Gita says that's proof you did the interview itself all wrong.
Stop caring at all. Evenness means you shouldn't even want this job in the first place.
chat.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna his right is to the work, not its fruits: act, and stay even in success and failure. That evenness is yoga.

tie.story: On the battlefield, Krishna told Arjuna to do his work without clinging to the result, even in success and failure.
tie.friend: Zoe did her part in the interview; she can wait for the call evenly instead of refreshing.
